title: Check yourself: Plan mode or direct execution

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A developer must replace a logging library that appears in forty-five source files, and two target designs would both work. How should the session begin?

options.text: Straight to editing, starting with a few of the files
options.says: Ruled out because the table says of a many-file change that "a wrong pattern is repeated everywhere", so the first files would commit the whole codebase.

options.text: Plan mode first, with the approach settled before any edit
options.says: Many files and several valid approaches both argue for planning first.

options.text: Straight to editing, then a plan once ten files are done
options.says: Ruled out because the documented workflow "separates research from implementation so that the work solves the right problem", which a late plan cannot do.

options.text: Plan mode only if the library is security-sensitive
options.says: Ruled out because "Importance is not a signal", and the signals are scope and the number of approaches.

origin.section: When a plan earns its cost

questions.stem: A stack trace points at one function that divides by zero when a list is empty. How should the fix be handled?

options.text: In plan mode, with a plan approved before any bug fix
options.says: Ruled out because "Plan mode is useful, but also adds overhead", and a small clear fix does not repay it.

options.text: In plan mode, with the division reviewed as a risky operation
options.says: Ruled out because "Two signals decide it: the number of files and the number of valid approaches", and risk is neither.

options.text: After an interview about the feature that owns the function
options.says: Ruled out because an interview suits a large unclear feature, and here "If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan".

options.text: Directly, then confirm with a test of that edge case
options.says: One file with a clear trace is the guide's example of direct execution.
